notes.text: Paywalls and offers: see the paywall canvas

iPhone flow (and iPad, same app):
1 First Connect: iOS shows its prompt at once. No screen of ours comes before it. This is how the app works today; it stays.
2 Don't Allow: the help sheet opens over Main. NEW. It replaces today's system alert "VPN configuration not added" (Try again / OK, MainScreen.VPNPermissionAlerts).
3 Try again: the sheet closes, then the app asks again, and iOS shows its prompt over Main (= frame 1). Allow → Connecting (current frame "Main · connecting"). Don't Allow again → the help sheet again.
4 ✕: the sheet closes. Back to Main, "Tap to connect" (current frame "Main · disconnected, free user"). The next Connect asks again. Nothing is remembered from a decline.
5 A management profile can block new VPN configurations; then iOS shows no prompt and the press ends as a decline. The last line of the help says where to look.
Not changed: the 20-second alert "Could not start the connection" (VPN-342).
Replaces: the system alert above. It has no frame on this canvas, so no current frame goes away on the iPhone and iPad pages.
The last line of the help after a decline (iPhone, iPad) is not built (board, 2026-11-18).

Texts — EN | AR. (app) = already in the app (Localizable.xcstrings), same EN and AR. (new) = new text. (system) = text of iOS or macOS, not ours.
Help after a decline, iPhone and iPad:
• VPN configuration not added | لم تتم إضافة إعداد VPN (app: VPN_PERMISSION.DENIED_TITLE)
• Securefield can't connect without a VPN configuration. Tap Try again and choose Allow. | لا يمكن لـ Securefield الاتصال بدون إعداد VPN. اضغط «حاول مرة أخرى» واختر «سماح». (app: perm.deniedBody)
• The system window looks like this: | تظهر نافذة النظام هكذا: (new)
• 1 Tap Allow in the system window | اضغط «سماح» في نافذة النظام (app: perm.step1.ios)
• 2 Confirm with Face ID, Touch ID or your passcode | أكّد بـ Face ID أو Touch ID أو رمز الدخول (app: perm.step2.ios)
• 3 Securefield connects. Nothing else to set up | يتصل Securefield. لا يلزم أي إعداد آخر (app: perm.step3)
• If the iOS window doesn't appear, new VPN configurations may be blocked on this device; see Settings › General › VPN & Device Management. | إذا لم تظهر نافذة iOS، فقد تكون إضافة إعدادات VPN جديدة محظورة على هذا الجهاز؛ راجع الإعدادات › عام › VPN وإدارة الجهاز. (new: the second half of VPN_PERMISSION.DENIED_MESSAGE as its own line)
• Try again | حاول مرة أخرى (app: VPN_PERMISSION.TRY_AGAIN)
• ✕ = Close, as on the Report sheet (no visible text).
Help after a decline, Mac:
• VPN configuration not added | لم تتم إضافة إعداد VPN (app: perm.deniedTitle)
• Securefield can't connect without a VPN configuration. Click Try again and choose Allow. | لا يمكن لـ Securefield الاتصال بدون إعداد VPN. انقر «حاول مرة أخرى» واختر «سماح». (new: Mac wording; perm.deniedBody says "Tap")
• The system window looks like this: | تظهر نافذة النظام هكذا: (new, the same text as above)
• 1 Click Allow in the macOS window | انقر «سماح» في نافذة macOS (app: perm.step1.mac)
• 2 Confirm with Touch ID or your Mac password | أكّد بـ Touch ID أو كلمة مرور جهاز Mac (app: perm.step2.mac)
• Try again | حاول مرة أخرى (app: perm.tryAgain)
• Open System Settings | فتح إعدادات النظام (app: perm.openSettings)
• Not now | ليس الآن (app text: CONNECTION_RATING.SKIP; new on the Mac)
System prompt (system; stand-in until the real screenshot, AR wording to confirm from it):
• “Securefield VPN” Would Like to Add VPN Configurations | يريد “Securefield VPN” إضافة إعدادات VPN
• All network activity on this iPhone (iPad, Mac) may be filtered or monitored when using VPN. | قد تتم تصفية كل نشاط الشبكة على هذا الـ iPhone (iPad، Mac) أو مراقبته عند استخدام VPN.
• Don’t Allow | عدم السماح   • Allow | سماح
No longer shown: perm.title, perm.body.mac, perm.step3 on the Mac, perm.continue (the Mac step before the prompt) and VPN_PERMISSION.DENIED_MESSAGE (the iPhone and iPad alert). The keys can stay.

The prompt picture. The board asked for the real iOS prompt picture. No screenshot of it is on the runner, and the runner may not open Apple pages. So every prompt in these frames (over the screens and inside the help) is a STAND-IN drawing in the dark look. Before the build, SecurefieldiOS takes the real prompt on SecureField's own test devices (iPhone, iPad and Mac), EN and AR, and the help uses a crop of it as an image asset (Assets › Images, one per platform and language). I then swap the drawing for the crop on this canvas. The green ring around Allow is ours (lightGreen #35DF91, 2.5 px, radius 12), drawn over the crop.

Tokens and components: GradientBackground; the Report sheet (iPhone radius 40/40/60/60, iPad form sheet radius 12); GradientBorderCard (iceBlue, radius 18, border gradient); the PermissionView step circles (darkBlue #0073C5, 26 pt, white bold); text lightGray #D1DCEA and white; RadialGradientButton green; Mac: PrimaryButtonStyle (#33A9FE → #1EB972), links lightGreen. No new token. New component: PromptPicture (card + crop of the system prompt + ring on Allow).
Contrast: white on darkBlue 4.93:1; lightGray on the card 7.72:1; lightGreen on the background 9.25:1. Below 4.5:1, kept exact because they are the app's own buttons: white on the green button 2.37:1, white on the Mac button 2.55:1 (see Proposals on VPN-907).

Approved, not built — VPN-924 · VPN-907 (below): after Don't Allow, a help sheet opens over Main. It replaces the system alert "VPN configuration not added" (not drawn on this canvas). These Main frames stay.

No-prompt flow (iPhone and iPad):
1 Connect: the app asks iOS for the VPN configuration.
2 iOS shows no prompt (for example a management profile blocks new VPN configurations, or iOS cannot load or save the configuration). The build tells this apart from a decline: refused while the app stayed active, or a load or save error = no prompt → THIS sheet over Main. Refused while the app was inactive (the prompt was up) = decline → the round-1 help sheet.
3 Try again: the sheet closes and the app asks again at once. The prompt shows (round-1 frame 1), or this sheet comes again.
4 ✕: the sheet closes. Back to Main, "Tap to connect". The next Connect asks again.
In the iOS Simulator every Connect ends here (the Simulator never shows the VPN prompt). Design review and QA see this screen first.
Scrolling (approval item 41, build rule in VPN-924): the content scrolls only when it does not fit; Try again stays fixed. These frames show the case that fits.
Replaces: no current frame. Today this case ends in the system alert "VPN configuration not added", which has no frame on this canvas.

Texts — EN | AR. (app) = already in the app (Localizable.xcstrings), same EN and AR. (new) = new text.
iPhone and iPad:
• iOS didn't show the VPN window | لم يعرض iOS نافذة VPN (new)
• New VPN configurations may be blocked on this device. | قد تكون إضافة إعدادات VPN جديدة محظورة على هذا الجهاز. (new: the first half of the approved round-1 help line)
• See | راجع (new, from the approved help line)
• Settings › General › VPN & Device Management | الإعدادات › عام › VPN وإدارة الجهاز (new, from the approved help line; the iOS path)
• Try again | حاول مرة أخرى (app: VPN_PERMISSION.TRY_AGAIN)
• ✕ = Close, as on the Report sheet (no visible text).
Mac:
• macOS didn't show the VPN window | لم يعرض macOS نافذة VPN (new)
• New VPN configurations may be blocked on this device. | قد تكون إضافة إعدادات VPN جديدة محظورة على هذا الجهاز. (new, the same text as above)
• See | راجع (new, the same text as above)
• System Settings › General › Device Management | إعدادات النظام › عام › إدارة الجهاز (new) — TO BE CHECKED ON THE MAC. This is the macOS 15 path (from web search results). The app runs from macOS 14; on macOS 14 the profiles are in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Profiles. The AR names must match the Arabic macOS menus.
• Try again | حاول مرة أخرى (app: perm.tryAgain)
• Open System Settings | فتح إعدادات النظام (app: perm.openSettings)
• Not now | ليس الآن (app text: CONNECTION_RATING.SKIP; new on the Mac in round 1)
In Arabic the › marks mirror on their own (Unicode mirrored character); the path reads right to left.

Parts and tokens: the round-1 help on each device. iPhone: the Report sheet (radius 40/40/60/60). iPad: the Report form sheet, 580 × 658 pt as today (this content fits; the round-1 help needs 760). Type × 1.3 on the iPad (Theme.typography). Mac: the round-1 Mac help window (480 × 640 + title bar).
In place of the prompt picture: the app's own Warning icon (assets/Icons/Warning.png, the main header report button), template, white (Theme.icon.primary), 44 pt (iPad 57 pt), in a GradientBorderCard (iceBlue, radius 18) on iPhone and iPad and in the round-1 Mac card.
Text: title NAMU-1850 white; line Red Hat Display lightGray #D1DCEA; path Red Hat Display bold white; button RadialGradientButton green (iPhone, iPad), PrimaryButtonStyle #33A9FE → #1EB972 (Mac); links lightGreen #35DF91. No new token, no new component, no new asset.
Contrast: lightGray on the card 7.72:1; white text and the white icon on the card 10.72:1 (at its lightest point); Mac card (white 6 %): white 13.48:1, lightGray 9.72:1; lightGreen on the background 9.25:1. Below 4.5:1, kept exact (the app's own buttons): white on the green button 2.37:1; white on the Mac button 2.55:1 — if the board approves VPN-923, the Mac button takes its new look here too.
Check: the iPhone sheet fits iPhone SE (375 × 667) in EN and AR without scrolling (rendered, not on the canvas).

Proposal — VPN-1058: the premium icon in place of the "PREMIUM" tag (board, 11-21).
Where: each premium row in the free user's server list (ServerItem, ServerListScreen.swift). Today the PremiumMark pill (SERVER_LIST.PREMIUM_MARK, "PREMIUM" / "مميز") sits before the signal bars. The proposal puts the icon in the same place. Flag, name, signal bars, radio button and spacing (12 pt while the mark shows) stay as today.
Icon: Design System icons/Premium (assets/Icons/Premium.svg, the app asset icons/Premium). It is the crown at the top left of the iPhone Main screen, the free user's way to Premium. So the user already knows it as "premium".
Size: 20 × 20 pt, scaledToFit. That is the height of today's pill (Caption line, 2 pt padding top and bottom), so the row height (63 pt on a 390 pt phone) and the alignment do not change. The signal bars are 25.2 pt and the radio 29.4 pt, so the crown stays the smallest mark in the row.
Colour: the asset's own stroke, lightYellow #FAC762 (text.quaternary / border.secondary, the premium colour; the orange radio ring of the same row has it). No tint. Contrast on the page background (#172231 to #000000): 10.2:1 to 13.4:1, above 3:1 for icons.
Arabic: the crown is symmetric and is not mirrored. In RTL it stays before the signal bars in reading order (left of them on screen).
Who sees it: only a free user, only on a premium server (Server.showsPremiumMark). A premium user sees no tag today and no icon in the proposal. Tap on the row opens the Premium screen, as today.
Not changed: the two-column iPad list (WideServerList, heading "Premium" with a crown), the Mac app, the onboarding.

VoiceOver (step 3).
Today: the row is one button. VoiceOver reads the name and the tag text: "Netherlands, PREMIUM, button" / "هولندا، مميز، زر".
Proposal: the icon gets an accessibility label with the same catalog text, SERVER_LIST.PREMIUM_MARK ("PREMIUM" / "مميز"). So VoiceOver reads the same words as today. No new text, no new translation.
Without a label, VoiceOver would read the asset name ("icons/Premium") or nothing. So the label is required.
Keep the accessibilityIdentifier "server_list.premium_mark" on the icon, so UI tests find it as today.
Proposal — VPN-1058 (below): the premium icon (icons/Premium, 20 pt) in place of the "PREMIUM" tag on locked rows. These free-user frames stay until the board approves.

notes.text: Approved, not built — VPN-924 (designs VPN-907 and VPN-907 NoPrompt), below. Proposals come after them.
Paywalls and offers: see the paywall canvas

iPad: the same flow as the iPhone (see the iPhone page): 1 Connect → iPadOS prompt at once; 2 Don't Allow → help sheet; Try again closes the sheet and asks again (= frame 1); ✕ → back to Main, "Tap to connect".
Sheet: a form sheet 580 pt wide, as the Report sheet. It is 760 pt high (Report: 658), because the help has more lines; in landscape it still fits between the status bar and the home indicator. Type × 1.3 (Theme.typography on a tablet). The prompt picture is not scaled.
Replaces: the system alert "VPN configuration not added" (no frame on this canvas). The Main frames stay.
The last line of the help after a decline (iPhone, iPad) is not built (board, 2026-11-18).

Texts — EN | AR. (app) = already in the app (Localizable.xcstrings), same EN and AR. (new) = new text. (system) = text of iOS or macOS, not ours.
Help after a decline, iPhone and iPad:
• VPN configuration not added | لم تتم إضافة إعداد VPN (app: VPN_PERMISSION.DENIED_TITLE)
• Securefield can't connect without a VPN configuration. Tap Try again and choose Allow. | لا يمكن لـ Securefield الاتصال بدون إعداد VPN. اضغط «حاول مرة أخرى» واختر «سماح». (app: perm.deniedBody)
• The system window looks like this: | تظهر نافذة النظام هكذا: (new)
• 1 Tap Allow in the system window | اضغط «سماح» في نافذة النظام (app: perm.step1.ios)
• 2 Confirm with Face ID, Touch ID or your passcode | أكّد بـ Face ID أو Touch ID أو رمز الدخول (app: perm.step2.ios)
• 3 Securefield connects. Nothing else to set up | يتصل Securefield. لا يلزم أي إعداد آخر (app: perm.step3)
• If the iOS window doesn't appear, new VPN configurations may be blocked on this device; see Settings › General › VPN & Device Management. | إذا لم تظهر نافذة iOS، فقد تكون إضافة إعدادات VPN جديدة محظورة على هذا الجهاز؛ راجع الإعدادات › عام › VPN وإدارة الجهاز. (new: the second half of VPN_PERMISSION.DENIED_MESSAGE as its own line)
• Try again | حاول مرة أخرى (app: VPN_PERMISSION.TRY_AGAIN)
• ✕ = Close, as on the Report sheet (no visible text).
Help after a decline, Mac:
• VPN configuration not added | لم تتم إضافة إعداد VPN (app: perm.deniedTitle)
• Securefield can't connect without a VPN configuration. Click Try again and choose Allow. | لا يمكن لـ Securefield الاتصال بدون إعداد VPN. انقر «حاول مرة أخرى» واختر «سماح». (new: Mac wording; perm.deniedBody says "Tap")
• The system window looks like this: | تظهر نافذة النظام هكذا: (new, the same text as above)
• 1 Click Allow in the macOS window | انقر «سماح» في نافذة macOS (app: perm.step1.mac)
• 2 Confirm with Touch ID or your Mac password | أكّد بـ Touch ID أو كلمة مرور جهاز Mac (app: perm.step2.mac)
• Try again | حاول مرة أخرى (app: perm.tryAgain)
• Open System Settings | فتح إعدادات النظام (app: perm.openSettings)
• Not now | ليس الآن (app text: CONNECTION_RATING.SKIP; new on the Mac)
System prompt (system; stand-in until the real screenshot, AR wording to confirm from it):
• “Securefield VPN” Would Like to Add VPN Configurations | يريد “Securefield VPN” إضافة إعدادات VPN
• All network activity on this iPhone (iPad, Mac) may be filtered or monitored when using VPN. | قد تتم تصفية كل نشاط الشبكة على هذا الـ iPhone (iPad، Mac) أو مراقبته عند استخدام VPN.
• Don’t Allow | عدم السماح   • Allow | سماح
No longer shown: perm.title, perm.body.mac, perm.step3 on the Mac, perm.continue (the Mac step before the prompt) and VPN_PERMISSION.DENIED_MESSAGE (the iPhone and iPad alert). The keys can stay.

The prompt picture. The board asked for the real iOS prompt picture. No screenshot of it is on the runner, and the runner may not open Apple pages. So every prompt in these frames (over the screens and inside the help) is a STAND-IN drawing in the dark look. Before the build, SecurefieldiOS takes the real prompt on SecureField's own test devices (iPhone, iPad and Mac), EN and AR, and the help uses a crop of it as an image asset (Assets › Images, one per platform and language). I then swap the drawing for the crop on this canvas. The green ring around Allow is ours (lightGreen #35DF91, 2.5 px, radius 12), drawn over the crop.

Tokens and components: GradientBackground; the Report sheet (iPhone radius 40/40/60/60, iPad form sheet radius 12); GradientBorderCard (iceBlue, radius 18, border gradient); the PermissionView step circles (darkBlue #0073C5, 26 pt, white bold); text lightGray #D1DCEA and white; RadialGradientButton green; Mac: PrimaryButtonStyle (#33A9FE → #1EB972), links lightGreen. No new token. New component: PromptPicture (card + crop of the system prompt + ring on Allow).
Contrast: white on darkBlue 4.93:1; lightGray on the card 7.72:1; lightGreen on the background 9.25:1. Below 4.5:1, kept exact because they are the app's own buttons: white on the green button 2.37:1, white on the Mac button 2.55:1 (see Proposals on VPN-907).

Approved, not built — VPN-924 · VPN-907 (below): after Don't Allow, a help sheet opens over Main. It replaces the system alert "VPN configuration not added" (not drawn on this canvas). These Main frames stay.

iPad: the same flow as the iPhone (see the iPhone page).
1 Connect: the app asks iOS for the VPN configuration.
2 iOS shows no prompt (for example a management profile blocks new VPN configurations, or iOS cannot load or save the configuration). The build tells this apart from a decline: refused while the app stayed active, or a load or save error = no prompt → THIS sheet over Main. Refused while the app was inactive (the prompt was up) = decline → the round-1 help sheet.
3 Try again: the sheet closes and the app asks again at once. The prompt shows (round-1 frame 1), or this sheet comes again.
4 ✕: the sheet closes. Back to Main, "Tap to connect". The next Connect asks again.
In the iOS Simulator every Connect ends here (the Simulator never shows the VPN prompt). Design review and QA see this screen first.
Scrolling (approval item 41, build rule in VPN-924): the content scrolls only when it does not fit; Try again stays fixed. These frames show the case that fits.
Replaces: no current frame. Today this case ends in the system alert "VPN configuration not added", which has no frame on this canvas.

Texts — EN | AR. (app) = already in the app (Localizable.xcstrings), same EN and AR. (new) = new text.
iPhone and iPad:
• iOS didn't show the VPN window | لم يعرض iOS نافذة VPN (new)
• New VPN configurations may be blocked on this device. | قد تكون إضافة إعدادات VPN جديدة محظورة على هذا الجهاز. (new: the first half of the approved round-1 help line)
• See | راجع (new, from the approved help line)
• Settings › General › VPN & Device Management | الإعدادات › عام › VPN وإدارة الجهاز (new, from the approved help line; the iOS path)
• Try again | حاول مرة أخرى (app: VPN_PERMISSION.TRY_AGAIN)
• ✕ = Close, as on the Report sheet (no visible text).
Mac:
• macOS didn't show the VPN window | لم يعرض macOS نافذة VPN (new)
• New VPN configurations may be blocked on this device. | قد تكون إضافة إعدادات VPN جديدة محظورة على هذا الجهاز. (new, the same text as above)
• See | راجع (new, the same text as above)
• System Settings › General › Device Management | إعدادات النظام › عام › إدارة الجهاز (new) — TO BE CHECKED ON THE MAC. This is the macOS 15 path (from web search results). The app runs from macOS 14; on macOS 14 the profiles are in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Profiles. The AR names must match the Arabic macOS menus.
• Try again | حاول مرة أخرى (app: perm.tryAgain)
• Open System Settings | فتح إعدادات النظام (app: perm.openSettings)
• Not now | ليس الآن (app text: CONNECTION_RATING.SKIP; new on the Mac in round 1)
In Arabic the › marks mirror on their own (Unicode mirrored character); the path reads right to left.

Parts and tokens: the round-1 help on each device. iPhone: the Report sheet (radius 40/40/60/60). iPad: the Report form sheet, 580 × 658 pt as today (this content fits; the round-1 help needs 760). Type × 1.3 on the iPad (Theme.typography). Mac: the round-1 Mac help window (480 × 640 + title bar).
In place of the prompt picture: the app's own Warning icon (assets/Icons/Warning.png, the main header report button), template, white (Theme.icon.primary), 44 pt (iPad 57 pt), in a GradientBorderCard (iceBlue, radius 18) on iPhone and iPad and in the round-1 Mac card.
Text: title NAMU-1850 white; line Red Hat Display lightGray #D1DCEA; path Red Hat Display bold white; button RadialGradientButton green (iPhone, iPad), PrimaryButtonStyle #33A9FE → #1EB972 (Mac); links lightGreen #35DF91. No new token, no new component, no new asset.
Contrast: lightGray on the card 7.72:1; white text and the white icon on the card 10.72:1 (at its lightest point); Mac card (white 6 %): white 13.48:1, lightGray 9.72:1; lightGreen on the background 9.25:1. Below 4.5:1, kept exact (the app's own buttons): white on the green button 2.37:1; white on the Mac button 2.55:1 — if the board approves VPN-923, the Mac button takes its new look here too.
Check: the iPhone sheet fits iPhone SE (375 × 667) in EN and AR without scrolling (rendered, not on the canvas).

Proposal — VPN-1058: the premium icon in place of the "PREMIUM" tag (board, 11-21).
Where: each premium row in the free user's server list (ServerItem, ServerListScreen.swift). Today the PremiumMark pill (SERVER_LIST.PREMIUM_MARK, "PREMIUM" / "مميز") sits before the signal bars. The proposal puts the icon in the same place. Flag, name, signal bars, radio button and spacing (12 pt while the mark shows) stay as today.
Icon: Design System icons/Premium (assets/Icons/Premium.svg, the app asset icons/Premium). It is the crown at the top left of the iPhone Main screen, the free user's way to Premium. So the user already knows it as "premium".
Size: 20 × 20 pt, scaledToFit. That is the height of today's pill (Caption line, 2 pt padding top and bottom), so the row height (63 pt on a 390 pt phone) and the alignment do not change. The signal bars are 25.2 pt and the radio 29.4 pt, so the crown stays the smallest mark in the row.
Colour: the asset's own stroke, lightYellow #FAC762 (text.quaternary / border.secondary, the premium colour; the orange radio ring of the same row has it). No tint. Contrast on the page background (#172231 to #000000): 10.2:1 to 13.4:1, above 3:1 for icons.
Arabic: the crown is symmetric and is not mirrored. In RTL it stays before the signal bars in reading order (left of them on screen).
Who sees it: only a free user, only on a premium server (Server.showsPremiumMark). A premium user sees no tag today and no icon in the proposal. Tap on the row opens the Premium screen, as today.
Not changed: the two-column iPad list (WideServerList, heading "Premium" with a crown), the Mac app, the onboarding.

VoiceOver (step 3).
Today: the row is one button. VoiceOver reads the name and the tag text: "Netherlands, PREMIUM, button" / "هولندا، مميز، زر".
Proposal: the icon gets an accessibility label with the same catalog text, SERVER_LIST.PREMIUM_MARK ("PREMIUM" / "مميز"). So VoiceOver reads the same words as today. No new text, no new translation.
Without a label, VoiceOver would read the asset name ("icons/Premium") or nothing. So the label is required.
Keep the accessibilityIdentifier "server_list.premium_mark" on the icon, so UI tests find it as today.
Proposal — VPN-1058 (below): the premium icon (icons/Premium, 20 pt) in place of the "PREMIUM" tag on locked rows. These free-user frames stay until the board approves.

notes.text: Approved, not built — VPN-924 (designs VPN-907 and VPN-907 NoPrompt) and VPN-981 (design VPN-923), below. Proposals come after them.
Paywalls and offers: see the paywall canvas

Panel footer: one new button, first in the row: "Open Securefield". It opens the main window and brings it to the front. Icon: SF Symbol macwindow, 15 pt, lightGray, like the other footer buttons. Shown in both modes (with and without the Dock icon).
Text: existing key menu.open — EN "Open Securefield", AR "فتح Securefield" (already in Localizable.xcstrings; not new). It is the button's tooltip and accessibility label.
Settings (gear) and Quit (power, "Quit Securefield") are already in this footer. No change to them.

VPN-795 — how the user gets menu-bar-only mode
RECOMMENDED (b): a "Show in Dock" switch in Settings, default on. Nothing changes for current users. A user who wants a menu-bar-only app turns it off.
Other options:
(a) Always menu-bar-only, no setting. Not recommended: every user loses the Dock icon, Command-Tab and the app menu; a new user may not find the app after first launch.
(c) Dock icon only while a Securefield window is open. Not recommended: the icon comes and goes, which looks unstable; it also needs the new panel button.
(b) with default off is possible. Then first launch changes, and I add a first-launch hint frame (new text).

Every place that changes when "Show in Dock" is off:
• Main window at launch: it does not open when the Mac opens the app at login (Open at login). It opens when the user opens the app (Finder, Launchpad, Spotlight). If the code cannot tell a login launch from a user launch, it opens at every launch, as today.
• Open the main window again: new panel button "Open Securefield" (frames above). Opening the app again from Finder, Launchpad or Spotlight also opens it. There is no Dock icon to click.
• Settings: panel gear and main-window toolbar gear, as today. Command-comma works only while a Securefield window is in front.
• Quit: panel power button "Quit Securefield", as today. Closing the windows does not quit, as today.
• Help, Report, Premium, Connect: in the panel and the main window, as today. The app menu and the Connection menu are not visible, so their shortcuts have no visible menu.
• First launch: no change (default on). Welcome and VPN permission open as today.
• Command-Tab: Securefield is not in it. Each button that opens a window brings it to the front.
No change: main window, first launch, report, FAQ and document windows, the iPhone and iPad pages.

Mac flow:
1 First launch: Welcome (privacy, current frame, no change) → the main window. The step "Allow the VPN configuration" is REMOVED: no screen of ours before the prompt.
2 First Connect: macOS shows its prompt over the main window. The Mac is premium only: a free user's Connect opens the paywall first, as today, so the prompt comes at the first Connect after premium. The frame shows a premium user (crowns, no Get Premium card).
3 Don't Allow: the window shows the help. It replaces "First launch · permission denied". Try again → the macOS prompt again. Open System Settings → the VPN page, as today. Not now (NEW) → the main window, Connect; the next Connect asks again.
Today the Mac asks for the permission from the first-launch step, before premium (MacRootView.requestPermission). After this change it asks from Connect (MacLive.toggle).
The frames use today's main window. VPN-809 (window without top bar) is built (VPN-810, 7.6): the prompt sits over that window form; nothing else changes.
Replaces: Mac "First launch · VPN permission" EN and AR (removed) and "First launch · permission denied" EN and AR (replaced by frame 2).

Texts — EN | AR. (app) = already in the app (Localizable.xcstrings), same EN and AR. (new) = new text. (system) = text of iOS or macOS, not ours.

System prompt (system; stand-in until the real screenshot, AR wording to confirm from it):
• “Securefield VPN” Would Like to Add VPN Configurations | يريد “Securefield VPN” إضافة إعدادات VPN
• All network activity on this iPhone (iPad, Mac) may be filtered or monitored when using VPN. | قد تتم تصفية كل نشاط الشبكة على هذا الـ iPhone (iPad، Mac) أو مراقبته عند استخدام VPN.
• Don’t Allow | عدم السماح   • Allow | سماح
No longer shown: perm.title, perm.body.mac, perm.step3 on the Mac, perm.continue (the Mac step before the prompt) and VPN_PERMISSION.DENIED_MESSAGE (the iPhone and iPad alert). The keys can stay.

The prompt picture. The board asked for the real iOS prompt picture. No screenshot of it is on the runner, and the runner may not open Apple pages. So every prompt in these frames (over the screens and inside the help) is a STAND-IN drawing in the dark look. Before the build, SecurefieldiOS takes the real prompt on SecureField's own test devices (iPhone, iPad and Mac), EN and AR, and the help uses a crop of it as an image asset (Assets › Images, one per platform and language). I then swap the drawing for the crop on this canvas. The green ring around Allow is ours (lightGreen #35DF91, 2.5 px, radius 12), drawn over the crop.

Tokens and components: GradientBackground; the Report sheet (iPhone radius 40/40/60/60, iPad form sheet radius 12); GradientBorderCard (iceBlue, radius 18, border gradient); the PermissionView step circles (darkBlue #0073C5, 26 pt, white bold); text lightGray #D1DCEA and white; RadialGradientButton green; Mac: PrimaryButtonStyle (#33A9FE → #1EB972), links lightGreen. No new token. New component: PromptPicture (card + crop of the system prompt + ring on Allow).
Contrast: white on darkBlue 4.93:1; lightGray on the card 7.72:1; lightGreen on the background 9.25:1. Below 4.5:1, kept exact because they are the app's own buttons: white on the green button 2.37:1, white on the Mac button 2.55:1 (see Proposals on VPN-907).

Approved, not built — VPN-924 · VPN-907 (below) replaces two frames of this row: "VPN permission" EN and AR are removed (no step before the macOS prompt), and "permission denied" EN and AR are replaced by the help after a decline. Welcome stays.

VPN-923 — Mac primary button: contrast per state (WCAG 2.x; text Red Hat Display Bold 15 pt = normal text, needs 4.5:1).
Measured from the values, at every point of the gradient; for pressed and disabled the button is laid over the window background (graphite #172231 → black), and the worst point counts.

TODAY (white text, #FFFFFF):
• normal: 2.55:1 (lightBlue end 2.55, green end 2.55, middle 2.59) — FAIL
• pressed (opacity 0.85): 2.40:1 worst point — FAIL
• disabled (opacity 0.4): 1.75:1 worst point — FAIL (WCAG does not require contrast for a disabled control; the board asked for 4.5:1 in every state)

PROPOSAL (drawn in these frames):
• normal: text graphite #172231 on lightBlue #33A9FE → green #1EB972: 6.15:1 worst point (6.30 at the blue end, 6.29 at the green end) — PASS
• pressed: as today, opacity 0.85 and scale 0.98: 4.79:1 worst point — PASS
• disabled: fill surfaceHigh (white 10 %, no gradient), text lightGray #D1DCEA: 8.54:1 over graphite, 12.61:1 over black — PASS
Pixel check on the renders of these 16 frames (Chromium; solid text colour against the fill at each column under the label; worst column): normal 6.10–6.16:1; pressed 4.74–4.81:1 (Welcome lowest: the map shows through); disabled 11.07:1. Today's frames, same check: 2.58:1.

Why dark text and not a darker gradient:
• Dark text keeps the brand gradient exactly, and it uses an existing token (graphite). The app already has a dark-text button: PremiumButtonStyle (#1B1305 on the yellow gradient).
• A darker gradient needs two new colours. darkBlue #0073C5 → darkGreen #198F57 gives only 4.11:1 at the green end. #0073C5 → #167F4E passes at rest (4.93) but fails when pressed (4.38).
Tokens: lightBlue, green, graphite, surfaceHigh, lightGray. No new token.

• PrimaryButtonStyle (native/Design/Brand.swift): .foregroundStyle(Brand.graphite) when enabled. Disabled: Capsule fill Brand.surfaceHigh and text Brand.lightGray, in place of .opacity(0.4). Pressed: no change.

• A ProgressView in the button (Report, while sending) takes the same disabled fill.

Text: title NAMU-1850 white; line Red Hat Display lightGray #D1DCEA; path Red Hat Display bold white; button RadialGradientButton green (iPhone, iPad), PrimaryButtonStyle #33A9FE → #1EB972 (Mac); links lightGreen #35DF91. No new token, no new component, no new asset.
Contrast: lightGray on the card 7.72:1; white text and the white icon on the card 10.72:1 (at its lightest point); Mac card (white 6 %): white 13.48:1, lightGray 9.72:1; lightGreen on the background 9.25:1. Below 4.5:1, kept exact (the app's own buttons): white on the green button 2.37:1; white on the Mac button 2.55:1 — if the board approves VPN-923, the Mac button takes its new look here too.

notes.text:
Products and offers — App Store Connect (asc-products on VPN-731, read 2026-11-12 18:27 UTC) and Adapty (export 2026-11-12 09:41Z). 1 of 3; prices and offers are in the next two notes.
Prices on the frames are samples: App Store sandbox prices in the app screenshots, Adapty's sample values in the Adapty previews. The App Store sets the real price per country. Adapty's USD value is not the store price.
All 8 products are auto-renewable subscriptions in the group "Premium Membership". iPhone, iPad and Mac use the same products (one app record). No non-subscription in-app purchase.
Placements: as Adapty names them. (B) = Paywall Builder placement. On iPhone a push shows its Adapty layout when its products load. If they do not load, and always on iPad, the app shows its own Premium screen with the HOME_TOP_LEFT_PREMIUM plans (Yearly, Monthly, Weekly).

• com.yearlyMembership — Yearly — 1 year — group level 1. Intro: none. Promotional: pay up front for the first year ("%50OFF" by its name). Win-back: 3 months free. Apple's cancel screen (Retention Messaging). App Store Connect → the subscription group → Retention Messaging; drafts made in VPN-1019, nothing live.
Where: the user taps Cancel Subscription in the App Store's subscription settings (iPhone, iPad, Mac with macOS 14+). Apple draws the whole screen; we give a header, a text and one image (or an offer).
Who sees the image: only when no offer shows. M3 (Yearly, 6-month): always. M1 (Weekly), M2 (Monthly): users who cannot get the offer: trial users, less than 1 paid month, Kuwait, an offer in the last 6 months. Most viewers are trial users who cancel (about 246 a week, mostly the Gulf and Jordan).
One image for all 3 messages: it has no words, so English and Arabic readers see the same image; the three messages share one promise (a private connection on every network), so there is nothing to show per plan. Apple allows only one image per message, the same for every language.
What it is: the app's splash, in 16:9. The app's page background (gradient-background #172231 → #000000, corner to corner, with World-Map.png in overlay blend, as GradientBackground.swift) and the splash logo (Lotties/Logo.json, last frame, rendered as vector at 50 % of the width, centred). Users know it from every app start. No prices, no offer marks, no words except the SecureField word-mark, no part of Apple's screens.
File: design-paywalls/assets/retention/SecureField-RetentionMessage-3840x2160.png · 3840 × 2160 · PNG, RGB, no alpha channel · 2.5 MB. SecurefieldiOS adds it to M1, M2 and M3 after the board approves. Apple's alt text: not asked for in App Store Connect (the API needs it: "SecureField").

How to read these frames: Apple draws this screen, not the app. Layout from third-party screenshots of Apple's cancel screen (RevenueCat blog, 2025); no Apple page was opened.
Apple's own texts (Confirm Cancellation, the end-date line, From the developer, Cancel Subscription, Keep Subscription): Apple writes them. The Arabic of Apple's texts here is our approximation, not Apple's string. The date is a sample.
Our texts: the VPN-1019 drafts, exact. Header above the text (Apple's default position), the image above both. Arabic: Apple sets right to left; the image is not mirrored.
Apple's screen follows the device: dark and light are both shown. Font: Apple's system font (SF Pro, SF Arabic); the runner has no Apple fonts, so the renders use a fallback.
Apple shows the image 16:9 with rounded corners; the logo stays well inside the edges, so a small crop loses nothing.

Questions and data gaps (for the board and the operator, through Project Manager).
1. Audience data that Adapty may not have. The operator confirms each, or the app or the backend must send it as a custom attribute:
• “Trial used, never paid” (audience 4): Adapty segments can filter on subscription state, but “had a trial, no paid period” is not a standard filter.
• “Paid 1–7 times” and “paid 8 or more times” (audiences 2 and 3): Adapty has total revenue, not a payment count. Proposal: the backend sets a custom attribute (for example paid_periods) from our webhook data.
• “5 or more days with a tunnel” (audience 5): Adapty does not know tunnel days. Needs a custom attribute (for example tunnel_days) from the app or the backend.
• Users whose payment failed: kept out of every offer audience (board, 2026-11-20).
• Country gate: needs a country filter per audience (Adapty has country; the operator updates it when the daily check changes).
2. The yearly win-back offer 599380d9 is Apple's win-back offer “Yearly Win Back Offer” (3 months free). Apple gives it only to users who paid at least 3 months and lapsed 6–24 months ago (asc-products, VPN-727). Users who lapsed 0–90 days ago (card C1) do not get it: they see the “no offer” frame (full yearly price). Board answer (2026-11-20): choice a. Apple's win-back offer only for users whom Apple finds eligible; all others see the yearly price with no offer.
3. 30 days free (8eff407d) is a promotional offer: only users who had a subscription can redeem it. Audience 3 has only paid users, so it fits. Never show it to audience 4.
4. “First month −50 %” on Monthly is a new promotional offer. The operator creates it in App Store Connect and Adapty; its id goes into the build sheet.
5. “Update payment”: not needed (board, 2026-11-20: no Payment failed screen).
6. No flow shows to premium users.

No new design for iPad in this task.
Effect: an iPad user in audiences 2–5 sees no offer. A promotional offer applies only if Adapty attaches it to the product (then the card shows the offer price; see the products note on the iPhone page). Users whose payment failed see the same Premium screen with no offer (board, 2026-11-20: no Payment failed screen).
Proposal for later (not in this task): if the board wants these offers on iPad, SecurefieldiOS turns AdaptyUI on for iPad or the app draws the variant; size M.

notes.text: Mac — no Adapty UI and no push. The app draws its own paywall with the HOME_TOP_LEFT_PREMIUM products. A new Adapty paywall never shows on the Mac.

Plans loaded: app screenshot. Loading, load failed and purchase message: an off-screen render of the app's own paywall view from a local build (not the store app). The purchase message uses the render's sample plans ($47.99 / year with a 3-day trial, $7.99 / month).

Deferred (board, 2026-11-20): the board deferred the Mac item until it asks again (then with no Payment failed state). Nothing here is built. Users whose payment failed see today's Mac paywall with no offer.
Mac: no Adapty layout and no push. The Mac app draws its own paywall (MacApp/MacPaywall.swift) with the products of placement HOME_TOP_LEFT_PREMIUM. Its title and feature lines can already come from the placement's remote config (keys “title” and “features”). So an Adapty audience on HOME_TOP_LEFT_PREMIUM can give the Mac these variants, with the same audience order as on the iPhone page.
Drawn from the code: 480 × 640 window, background #0F3A4D → #172231 → #000000 (top to bottom), App-Logo 34 pt, headline NAMU-1850 22, feature rows (✓ in a 26 pt circle, lightGreen at 14 %), plan cards (padding 16, radius 16; selected: lightYellow 2 pt border, lightYellow at 8 %), PremiumButtonStyle (52 pt capsule, lightYellow → darkYellow, text #1B1305), Restore · Terms of Use · Privacy Policy, fine print in mediumGray. The ✓ and the close ✕ are SF Symbols in the app (checkmark, xmark.circle.fill); the frames show a text stand-in. Content below 640 pt scrolls.
What works today with remote config only: title, the three feature lines, the product order (Monthly first), Subscribe, the free-trial lines of a free-trial offer (8eff407d, 599380d9) if Adapty attaches the offer to the product on the Mac.
What needs an app change (SecurefieldiOS; proposal, size M):
1. The line under the features is fixed today (“Securefield for Mac is a Premium service. Try it free first.”). It must come from remote config (new key “subtitle”); “Keep Premium for less” must not say “free”.
2. A pay-up-front or pay-as-you-go offer (first month −50 %, the two intro products) shows only the full price today: the card needs “First month [offer price]” / “First year [offer price]” and a matching fine print (3 new strings).
3. The free-trial fine print says “per year” for every plan; for Monthly it must say “per month” (1 new string).
4. Remote config is per placement: the Mac and the iPhone/iPad Premium screen share HOME_TOP_LEFT_PREMIUM, so these texts would also reach that screen if it reads them.
5. Win-back offers on the Mac need macOS 15 or later (StoreKit). SecurefieldiOS confirms.
Texts: the same new texts as on the iPhone page, plus the app's Mac strings (paywall.* in Localizable.xcstrings). New Mac-only strings: the fine-print lines “[offer price] for the first month, then [price] per month/year …”, “[offer price] for the first year …”, “After the free trial, [price] per month …”, and “First month [offer price]”, “First year [offer price]” (EN and AR on the frames).
